##  · D3-q-scope — D3: socket-capability representation, root scopes, grant, self-address set, IPv4/static/TCP-only

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 2

*Resolved in an earlier workspace; reopen it if the code has changed since.*

Evidence: Ruled (IPv4/TCP, args scopes, narrowing grant, self set first); implemented in ipd and merged at dc3c8aab1.

### D3 implementer · Question

Event: `3da5061ee3bcfcdab56c3a0cc61e0c92` · 2026-09-24T20:18:42Z

> **Spec.**
> - NAMESPACES: "Its scope is IP prefixes and ports only ... Session scopes never include the box's own addresses, including any address that routes back to the box (CAPABILITIES.md)."
> - INIT: principals carry a net scope; "ipd:lan delivers port 22 only to sshd (sole holder of 'listen TCP 22')".
> - WIRE: Granting and releasing.
> 
> **Unspecified**, with my recommendation for each:
> 
> 1. **Root scopes.** init mints ipd's badges, and ipd's arguments (server-defined, like keyd's name,purpose,seed) say what each root badge means: `scope=<badge>:c:0.0.0.0/0:1-65535` for the steward and `scope=<badge>:l:22` for sshd. `ingress=<badge>` marks netd's frame badge, which has no /net. Also `addr=10.0.2.15/24` and `gateway=10.0.2.2`. The configuration is static; there is no DHCP.
> 2. **Narrowing.**
>    - A typed `grant(scope: bytes) -> conn: handle[0] endpoint, id: u64`, opcode 16 in ipd's ninep table. Each rule must lie inside a held rule, so it can never widen or add listen.
>    - Release is ninep_common disconnect(id), which covers descendants and aborts their sockets.
>    - new_connection("") keeps the same scope.
>    - It needs a small additive libs/rt API, NineServer::mint_rooted, so grant and new_connection share one Minted table.
> 3. **Scope layout.** count: u8, then up to 8 rules of `kind u8 (1 connect, 2 listen), addr bytes[4], len u8, lo u16, hi u16`.
> 4. **Own addresses**, refused before and regardless of scope:
>    - the interface address, network and directed broadcast, 255.255.255.255;
>    - 127/8 and 0/8;
>    - 224/4 and 240/4;
>    - every manifest `self=` prefix. On QEMU that is 10.0.2.2/32: slirp maps it to host loopback, and hostfwd leads it back to guest :22.
> 
>    Stated residual: routes-back addresses outside the box (NAT hairpin) are refused only if listed.
> 5. **Listen ports** are held per root-badge lineage; another lineage gets in_use. Any remote may connect to a listener.
> 6. **IPv4 and TCP only** in D3.
> 
> **Decision needed.** Approve, or amend. The text goes to NAMESPACES/INIT with an ANSWERS record.
